practice_description.medium: Sound, AI voice models, installation, performance, software
practice_description.practice_summary: Composer and artist who trains custom AI voice models on consented vocal data, treating the entire model-making pipeline -- dataset creation, training, governance -- as creative work. Pioneer of protocol art where systems and infrastructure are the artistic medium.
practice_description.methodology: Herndon composes music specifically for training AI models, treating dataset creation as an artistic act. She holds 'training ceremonies' where live participants sing to her AI (Spawn), creating communal training data. She earned a doctorate at Stanford CCRMA researching IP implications of machine learning. Collaborates closely with Mat Dryhurst (partner), Jules LaPlace (developer), Never Before Heard Sounds (NYC), and Voctro Labs (Barcelona). Each stage of the process -- composing training material, recording datasets, training models, generating outputs -- is treated as a distinct creative intervention.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Herndon's practice exemplifies art-as-substrate: her voice models are instruments others compose with, and her governance systems (Holly+ DAO) demonstrate how creative identity can be collectively managed. Her work directly models how art can function as primary material in a graph-curated generative exhibition.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes -- Holly+ is literally a voice instrument that others use as substrate. Her trained voice model is raw material that anyone can feed audio into and receive transformed output. The model itself is the artwork, and all derivative works are built on this substrate layer.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes -- Holly+ DAO governance means the voice instrument's outputs are determined by relational decisions among token-holding stewards. The Call at Serpentine involved 15 choirs across the UK contributing to a shared choral AI model, with a data trust governing relationships between contributors.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Yes -- the AI models evolve as new training data is contributed (50,000+ voices have contributed to Spawn's training). The Call's interactive installation responded to visitor singing input in real time, creating new collaborative musical output through call-and-response with the AI.

works.title: PROTO
works.description: Album created with Spawn, an AI vocal neural network trained on Herndon's voice and a Berlin vocal ensemble through live 'training ceremonies'. Over 50,000 voices contributed to Spawn's training.
works.relevance: Pioneering example of communal AI training as artistic practice -- the dataset is the artwork. Demonstrates how collective vocal contribution can feed a generative system.

works.title: Holly+
works.description: DAO-governed AI voice instrument allowing anyone to upload audio and receive it transformed into Herndon's voice. Governed by token-holding stewards who vote on commercial uses.
works.relevance: Core example of protocol art: a creative identity governed as commons infrastructure. Directly models art-as-substrate where the voice model is raw material for others' compositions.

works.title: The Call (Serpentine, with Mat Dryhurst)
works.description: Immersive installation at Serpentine North featuring AI choral models trained on 15 UK community choirs singing a custom songbook of hymns. Visitors sang into microphones and the AI responded, creating collaborative music. Governed by a data trust experiment.
works.relevance: Most complete expression of their practice: composed training data, consented communal dataset, custom AI models, spatial audio installation, data trust governance, and interactive visitor participation -- all as a single artwork.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Herndon treats every layer of the AI pipeline as artistic medium: composing songs for training (not for human ears), designing recording protocols, building governance structures (DAO, data trusts), and creating consent frameworks. The technical and legal infrastructure IS the artwork -- systems that produce creative output rather than singular artifacts.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Holly+ voice instrument and DAO governance system; Spawn AI vocal network; The Call's choral data trust and recording protocol; co-founded Spawning AI (consent infrastructure for AI training data across the industry).

commons_orientation.licence_model: Hybrid -- Holly+ voice model is freely usable by anyone; commercial use requires DAO approval. Spawning AI tools are partly open-source. Revenue split: 50% creator, 40% DAO, 10% Holly.
commons_orientation.commons_summary: Herndon builds commons infrastructure at multiple scales: Holly+ makes her voice a public instrument governed collectively; Spawning AI builds industry-wide consent infrastructure (HaveIBeenTrained, ai.txt protocol, Source.Plus). She frames openness as conditional on consent -- 'more will opt in than out, but first we have to establish common respect.'

governance_model.governance_detail: Holly+ is governed by a DAO where ERC-20 VOICE token holders vote on commercial uses of the voice model. Revenue from approved works splits 50/40/10 (creator/DAO/Holly). DAO treasury funds creation of new instruments. The Call introduced a data trust model for choristers who contributed training data, distributing power between data contributors and model users. Herndon has stated that in the event of her death, she prefers distributed DAO ownership over traditional inheritance.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Consent is foundational. Training ceremonies for Spawn involve live, willing participants singing to the AI. The Call required explicit agreements with 15 choirs under a data trust. Spawning AI (co-founded by Herndon) builds consent infrastructure for the entire AI industry. Each contributor knows their data is being used for AI training.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Collaborative and distributed. Herndon is the originating voice but authorship is shared: anyone can create with Holly+, the DAO governs what counts as 'official', and the 50,000+ voice contributors to Spawn are acknowledged as co-creators. Machine co-authorship is explicit -- AI is treated as collaborator, not tool.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Holly+ is a persistent instrument that continues to generate new outputs as users upload audio. The AI models evolve with new training data contributions. The Call's installation responded to visitor input in real time. Herndon's practice is durational-infinite in ambition -- the DAO is designed to outlive her, and the voice model is meant to persist as a governed commons.

data_materiality.data_sources: Herndon's own singing and speaking voice (full English phoneme range via TIMIT scripts); 50,000+ contributed voices for Spawn; 15 UK community choirs singing custom hymnal songbook for The Call; Sacred Harp collection of 19th-century hymns.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Fully consented -- all vocal data is explicitly contributed through live training ceremonies, choir recording sessions with data trust agreements, or Herndon's own voice. No scraped data. The provenance chain is a core part of the artwork.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Herndon's voice models operate in latent vocal spaces where audio style transfer maps source audio characteristics onto her voice's learned representation. The neural networks encode vocal features into a latent space that enables texture mapping between voices. This is engagement with embedding/latent space as creative medium.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes -- spans audio (voice models, spatial sound), visual (AI-generated imagery for Whitney Biennial xHairyMutantx, engraved physical artifacts), text (hymnal songbooks), and performative/interactive elements.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: The Call at Serpentine transformed the gallery into a chapel-like immersive spatial audio environment with custom architectural objects (The Wheel chandelier, The Hearth organ-like instrument) designed by studio sub. Visitors physically sang into microphones to interact with the AI. Whitney Biennial included large-format digital prints and web-based AI chatbot. Live performances feature ensemble singing with AI.

interoperability.composability: High -- Holly+ is explicitly designed as an instrument for others to compose with. Upload any audio, receive transformed output. The voice model's outputs serve as inputs for others' creative work. The DAO creates a feedback loop where approved works fund new instruments.
interoperability.technical_openness: Partially open -- Holly+ instruments are freely accessible online. Spawning AI has open-source Python packages and public APIs. The voice model itself is accessible but governed by the DAO for commercial use.

technical_approach.stack: Deep neural networks for voice synthesis and audio style transfer; custom voice models developed with Voctro Labs (spin-off of UPF Music Technology Group, connected to VOCALOID development) and Never Before Heard Sounds; Ethereum blockchain for DAO governance (ERC-20 VOICE tokens); multi-channel recording protocol for choral datasets; real-time voice conversion; TIMIT scripts for phoneme coverage; OpenAI DALL-E 2 for visual materials.

network_position.scene_affiliation: AI art and music (central figure); Berlin electronic music and experimental art; Stanford CCRMA alumni network; Serpentine Arts Technologies; Web3/DAO art community; AI ethics and policy (TIME 100 most influential voices in AI, 2023); European digital arts (Ars Electronica STARTS Prize 2022, Austrian Digital Human Rights Award 2024, Kairos Prize 2025).
network_position.connections: Mat Dryhurst (partner, co-creator on all major works); Spawning AI / Source.Plus (co-founded); Holly+ (created); Interdependence podcast (co-host); Jules LaPlace (Spawn developer); Never Before Heard Sounds; Voctro Labs; Serpentine Galleries; Whitney Museum.

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Herndon's practice is a near-perfect case study for A(DAI)'s vision: art-first, commons-oriented, protocol-as-artwork, consented data, collective governance. She could serve as a conversation partner on governance models for creative AI, a theoretical reference for how art functions as infrastructure, or potentially contribute artwork-in-graph (Holly+ voice as a node in a generative composition). Her data trust experiments with The Call directly parallel A(DAI)'s ambitions.
